verdict.reasoning: Patient reports feeling unwell for 'a good few days' and later dates onset to Saturday, 'about five days ago', with cough, cold, runny nose, sore throat, and feeling run-down: 'I just feel a bit, run-down, you know I've got, a cough, a cold', 'bit of a runny, bit of a runny nose', 'I've had a bit of a sore throat'.

Patient states cough is mostly dry and worse in the morning with some sputum: 'mostly, dry... it's a wee bit in the morning it's a bit worse', and later acknowledges phlegm when asked 'So you're not bringing up any mucky, flem?' – 'yeah... it's a wee bit'.

When asked about breathing, patient initially says it's not good and confirms shortness of breath: 'No, no it's, it's, it's not, it's not good', 'you're feeling more short of breath?' – 'Yeah, yeah.' He denies chest pain: 'any pain in your chest at all?' – 'No, no... it's just a wee bit shortness of breath... it's not pain'.

Patient describes night sweats and temperature fluctuations: 'in bed with the wife and having to, you know get out and, get the blanket off, and put it back on again', after question about 'temperatures or fevers... feeling hot and cold? Sweaty?'. He has not measured temperature: 'I just feel it in my forehead but... I haven't... used a thermometer or anything.'
Patient reports early brief diarrhea, now resolved: 'the first day I had, you know a wee bit... a wee bit of diarrhoea... but that, that's, that's fine, now.'

Patient notes generalized stiffness involving elbows and knees: 'when I'm bending down and... moving about, it's just, a wee, a wee bit stiffer than, than normal', and when asked where, replies, 'when you're bending like, elbows and knees and just, just a wee bit, kinda stiff... all over.'
Patient explicitly reports diabetes: 'I've got the uh, I've got the diabetes.' Doctor clarifies type: 'What type... is it type one or type two?' Patient responds 'it's uh, type, two, two.'

Patient reports prior high blood pressure reading: 'he... took my blood pressure and that said that was, that was high, uh, high, higher than it should be.' Doctor paraphrases: 'You've been diagnosed with high blood pressure...'.
Patient lists Metformin: 'It's... Metformin?' Doctor confirms: 'that's correct, OK.'
Patient lists Lisinopril: 'and there's another one, Lisinopril? Is that? Yeah.' Doctor repeats: 'Lisinopril, yeah.'
Patient mentions intermittent Aspirin use: 'a wee bit of Aspirin or whatever every now and again, but you know nothing long-term.' This supports as-needed use.
When asked about allergies to medications, patient replies: 'No, nothing, nothing that, nothing that I'm aware of, doctor's never said nothing to me, so.'
Living and job are described: 'now it's just me and the missus', and 'there's a wee factory, just down the road... we just manufacture like... kind of steel, steel parts.'
Patient estimates alcohol intake: 'maybe what like four, four pints on like Saturday and then... on, Sunday as well... maybe like. Nine, nine pints in a week, I would say.'

Patient admits occasional smoking and vaping to cut down: 'a wee, every now and again, but I'm, I, I am trying to cut that down. I've got a wee... vaporisers... I've been cutting down on the cigarettes.'

Doctor’s assessment: 'I think you know what you essentially have is a bit of a, a bit of a viral illness perhaps, a bit of a, maybe early signs of a flu.' This is equivalent to viral URTI/early flu-like illness.
Transcript confirms T2DM and metformin use but never states control status: no wording like 'controlled' or HbA1c mentioned. Claim of being 'controlled' is an added inference.

Transcript confirms high blood pressure and lisinopril use but not level of control: 'that was high, higher than it should be' and current medication list. No statement that hypertension is controlled.

Alcohol and tobacco use are both reported: 'I do like a wee drink... maybe like... Nine, nine pints in a week', and 'a wee [smoke], every now and again... cutting down on the cigarettes... got myself one of those [vaporisers].'
Doctor advises nonpharmacologic care and paracetamol: 'stay rested, drink plenty of fluids', and 'if you are feeling hot and cold and sweaty, taking regular Paracetamol would be beneficial.'

Doctor outlines a delayed antibiotic plan: 'I'm a little bit on the edge about giving you antibiotics... what we could think about is giving you a script for antibiotics... give it about twenty four to forty eight hours. If you feel like you're still feeling breathless and, run-down... starting a course of antibiotics, something like Amoxicillin. One tablet, three times a day.'
Continuation of metformin is not explicitly discussed in the plan; medications are only listed, with no advice about changing or continuing diabetes therapy.
Similarly, there is no explicit instruction regarding continuing lisinopril; hypertension medications are listed but not addressed in the plan.
Doctor encourages smoking cessation: 'Well, I wish you all the best on your journey to quit, I highly recommend it. Um, if you can, it'll certainly help your health as well.'
Follow-up advice given: 'if you're still not better by next week, come back and see me, we can have another look.'
Doctor notes nasal congestion/sniffles during phone consult: 'Yeah, I can certainly hear you've got the sniffles. So, bit of a runny, bit of a runny nose, you mentioned.'
